text:
Brandon Hagel is the rare player whose points undersell him. He has 17 in 15 games, and NHL.com just named him the Lightning's best player of the month, which is fair. The underlying numbers are better still. Tampa Bay takes 61% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, yet his teammates have scored 9.3 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on. That gap usually swings back, and his points with it.

A sixth-round pick (159th overall in 2016) who never signed with Buffalo, Hagel has become a play driver by any measure. Evolving-Hockey had him 16th among 401 forwards last season at 2.9 wins above replacement, with his team creating 0.44 more expected goals per 60 with him on, 99th percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds 11.0 primary shot assists per 60 (97th percentile) and a steady diet of passes across the slot.

He has an edge, too: Sports Illustrated and others covered him taking a jab at Dylan Larkin amid the Nikita Kucherov trade drama. Our projection: 32 to 51 goals, 74 to 104 points.
headline: Hagel is better than his 17 points
